# Running the HyperFrames CLI

`<SKILLS>` is the folder that holds the loaded skill's folder. Every skill and reference writes
the CLI as `npx hyperframes` (or bare `hyperframes`). Run each of those commands as:

```bash
node "<SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" <command> <args...>
```

Run it in the user's project directory, never in the skills directory. npm starts in the home
folder, so the project's `package.json`, `node_modules` and `.npmrc` cannot choose the CLI or the
registry; the CLI then moves into the project and works there. This holds for every command,
including the usage beacon, and for a project the person received from someone else. Do not run
`npx hyperframes` in the project directly, and do not run a project's own scripts or wrappers in
its place unless the person asks for that command by name.

For bundled Node helpers, use the same launcher with
`--script <absolute-script-path> <args...>`. Helpers that call the CLI then run it through the
launcher.

## Standalone skill installs

Without a plugin manifest, the launcher runs the newest compatible published CLI. To select a
release, put `--cli-version latest` or `--cli-version <exact-version>` before the command.
Take an exact version from the person, from the version an upgrade moves the pins to, or from
`--cli-version latest --version`. Never take it from the project's own files: a `package.json`
pin does not choose the CLI unless the person asks for that release. The launcher refuses a release older than its floor (currently 0.9.80), the oldest one with
the protections for received projects, and its error names the floor.
Use the launcher from the loaded skill installation for commands shown in CLI output, too.
For example, run `node "<SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" --cli-version latest --version`
to read the current release. If the installed launcher lacks this option, ask the person to update
their skills. The person installs and
updates standalone skills with `npx hyperframes skills update`.

## Plugin installs

Check the directory two levels above the loaded `SKILL.md` for `plugin.json`,
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, or
`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` identifying `hyperframes`, or a Gemini extension manifest.
That directory is `<PLUGIN_ROOT>`, and `<SKILLS>` is `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/skills`.

Call the directory you run the launcher in the working directory. It is a plugin install only
when all three of these hold:

- The name of `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` does not start with a dot, so it is not `.agents` or `.claude`.
- `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` is not the working directory, and it does not contain it.
- If `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` is inside the working directory, a folder whose name starts with a dot
  lies between them, as `.claude` does in `~/.claude/plugins/...` when you work in `~`.

Otherwise the skills are a standalone install, and the launcher ignores any manifest there.
Ignore it too, and follow the standalone rules above. The launcher refuses a manifest that
pins a release older than its floor.

For a plugin installation, these rules also apply in every skill and reference:

- Do not run `hyperframes skills update`, `skills check`, or `npx skills add`.
  The agent's plugin manager owns installation and updates. Read the skill at
  `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; report a missing bundled skill instead
  of downloading a different release. Resolve all skill references inside this
  bundle, even if a standalone copy is also installed. Claude exposes the router
  as `/hyperframes:hyperframes`; other clients may expose `/hyperframes`.
- The launcher selects the manifest's CLI version and disables automatic standalone skill
  installation, including during `init`. The first call may download that exact
  CLI version through npm. A download failure is an error, not permission to use
  latest. Existing project dependency files and lockfiles must not be overwritten
  to match the plugin; surface a runtime incompatibility before changing them.
- For bundled Node helpers, the launcher also passes the release version to their
  dependency loader. External providers, registry downloads, and existing project
  dependencies have their own versions; a plugin version alone does not freeze those inputs.
- Treat the plugin directory as read-only. Put outputs and temporary work in the
  project or a temporary directory. Pass this plugin root and launcher convention
  to any delegated agent so it does not fall back to global skills.

Newer skills come through the client's plugin update flow and a session reload,
which the person runs. Do not update an installed plugin yourself.

The launcher suppresses CLI update notices as well as standalone skill refreshes, including when running an older CLI with a stale notice cache. It passes the release as `HYPERFRAMES_PLUGIN_VERSION` for plugin-aware helpers and as `HYPERFRAMES_SKILL_PKG_VERSION` for the existing helper-package bootstrap. Our release process versions those packages together.

# Making the episode

<!-- skill-scripts: relative-ok, kit tools run only from a template this session pulled and checked -->

The template holds every rule and tool; this file sets the order and the discipline. When this file and the template disagree, the template wins, except on the length the person picked (§3) and on Pro and credits (SKILL.md).

Order: `read → settle the voice → say what's coming → ask (only what is open) → facts + script → stop 1 (storyboard) → voice → face → footage → shot plan + build → checks → stop 2 (draft) → render → reply`

## 1. The template

- It is in `templates/<slug>/`: CHANNEL.md (the channel: identity, caption skin, title look, rights) and one `series/<series>/` folder with TEMPLATE.md, REMIX.md, voice.md, frame.md, editing.md, footage.md, sound.md and `kit/` (the starter project and its tools, with its fonts, sound and assets). A series built from components has `components/`; a drawn series has STYLE.md and `kit/engine/` instead.
- Where a template names something only the HyperFrames app has (`media.find`, `voice.cloneVoice`, the Storyboard tab), use its command-line route or what this file says.

## 2. Read in this order

1. CHANNEL.md.
2. `series/<series>/TEMPLATE.md`: what the episode is, its runtime, the slots, what topics it is good and not good for. A topic it is not good for: say so in one line and, in the same message, offer the nearest angle that fits. Never offer to make the unfit topic anyway.
3. `series/<series>/REMIX.md`. **Its step table is the process.** Follow it in order and skip nothing.
4. `series/<series>/kit/README.md`: the tools, their Python packages and the project they build.
5. Every other file when a REMIX.md step points to it. editing.md lists every component with the creator's own use of it; footage.md says what to show for each kind of line and where to find it.

## 3. What to ask, once

The person's message carries what it carries. Ask once, together, only what is still open: the topic, the length, the voice, for a presented series the face and, when no `PEXELS_API_KEY` is set and the template's footage.md uses Pexels, whether they'd add a free Pexels API key (pexels.com/api, a minute to get). It is optional: without it, footage comes from the other sources footage.md names.

- **Never the creator's face, voice, footage, wordmark or show name.** That rule is about the creator: the person's own clone, their own recording or a credited stock voice are all fine.
- **A presenter runs on the plan.** Their own HeyGen avatar if they have one (`npx hyperframes media-use avatars` lists the looks on the HyperFrames account making the film; never `heygen avatar list`, a separate sign-in that can be another account), otherwise Avatar IV from their photo, both through `npx hyperframes media-use generate --type avatar` with the finished voice, so the lips land on it. HeyGen Video 1 is the fallback when neither works.
- **Settle the voice before any research.** A HeyGen voice id the person gave, or an 8-character prefix of one, is used only when they say it is theirs, that its owner agreed to this film, or that it is a HeyGen stock voice. Having the id is not that, and an id missing from `npx hyperframes media-use voices` proves nothing (it lists one page), so when they have not said, ask it in the one round of questions. A prefix: find the full id in `npx hyperframes media-use voices --limit 100`, and ask when it matches none or several. A clone they name as theirs, or say its owner agreed to: find it there and use it. That list is every clone the HyperFrames account's workspace can use, a teammate's included, and does not say who made one, so never pick from it by count, language or name; never `heygen voice list`, a separate sign-in that can be another account. Nothing named, or not signed in: ask once for their voice id, a clone they make in HeyGen from 30 s to 3 min of their own reading, or their own recorded narration; with none of these, say in one line that you'll use a HeyGen stock voice, credit it as AI-generated, and go on. The credits line for any voice, a recording or another vendor included, is `voice_credit` in the audio run's `audio_meta.json`. Nothing is voiced for it before stop 1: at the voice step, `npx hyperframes media-use generate --type voice --voice <the script's language> --script "<first line>" --out .media/pick.mp3 --plan` names HeyGen's first public voice in that language without making anything; set the kit's voice id to its `voice_id` and credit that voice by name. Nothing else starts until this is settled.
- **Then say what's coming** in one short message that is not a question, and go on without waiting: the working title and hook, the length, and roughly how long it takes. No prices.
- **The length is the person's, and it beats the template's runtime.** Offer about 1 minute first: the cold open, the title beat and one chapter, the end card short. 2 to 4 minutes: REMIX.md's short cut. A full episode: the series' own runtime. Their own words ("90 seconds", "5 min"): that length. No length answered and none in the topic: about 1 minute, and offer the longer cut in the reply. Scale everything to it: script words (the template's script stats at that runtime), facts, sections, music cues, review rounds (one for a minute, two for a full episode); never pad or trim to reach the series' runtime instead.
- **Credits name only who the person names.** Roles and names come from the person, never from a voice list, an account or a placeholder; a role nobody named is left out.
- Everything else REMIX.md §0 asks (chapters, language) takes REMIX.md's default; write each one, and the length, with why, in the project's `CLAUDE.md`.

## 4. Facts and script, then stop 1

- Facts first, per REMIX.md: every number, date and quote with its source. A research sub-agent is fine.
- Write the script to voice.md and the series' script anatomy; run the script checks REMIX.md names.
- **Stop 1:** pose the script and the shot plan as stills on the board, written as the hyperframes skill's `references/storyboard.md` says: one still per beat, its line under it, what each shot shows and which component makes it. Never pay for a voice to get a board. A series kit builds its film from the voice's timing, so first give it estimated timing with the free route REMIX.md names for stop 1 (most kits: `python3 tools/voice.py --silent`, silent stand-ins at the series' pace), assemble, and pose in the `index.html` that builds, as `storyboard.md` says. A drawn series poses in the test shot its REMIX.md names instead. Every time on the board is an estimate until the voice exists; say so. Tell the person the board is in the Storyboard tab beside the preview, as `storyboard.md` says, and wait for their go.

## 5. Voice and face

- Voice: the person's voice id, through the kit's voice tool, as REMIX.md says. Then the kit's timing and pause tools. The voice is final before any presenter.
- **Audition before the whole script:** one paragraph (the kit's voice tool, as REMIX.md says), measure words a minute the way REMIX.md §0 measures them, and set the kit's `voice.speed` to land on the series' rate. The voice call itself takes no speed for an instant clone; the kit changes tempo locally from the kept native audio, so a new speed costs nothing. Past the range REMIX.md allows, change the words instead. Voice the script once; re-voice only the paragraphs that changed.
- Face (presented series): REMIX.md's host step, on the final voice: their own avatar, Avatar IV from their photo, or the HeyGen Video 1 fallback. Their own takes: cut them per editing.md's presenter rules.
- A changed line after the presenter take exists means the whole take is made again, or the lips drift.

## 6. Footage, shot plan, build

- Find footage per footage.md, from the sources it names (Wikimedia Commons, Openverse, NARA, Library of Congress, Prelinger, Pexels, Mixkit, official media). Download with curl. Pexels needs the person's free `PEXELS_API_KEY`; its web pages refuse an agent, so without a key go on to the next source. Check each clip's own licence (some Mixkit clips are Restricted). A site that refuses an agent (403, 429, a bot check): move to another source; never work around the check. One sub-agent per chapter is fine. Every file gets a licence line in the record REMIX.md names; credit what needs credit.
- Never take footage from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram or X unless its licence is stated.
- A real brand's logo or sign, and screenshots of web pages, appear only under terms that allow it (the template's rights rules, a press kit's terms, a stated licence); otherwise crop it out, cite the page as a source line, or leave it out, and say so in the reply. Where REMIX.md asks to search YouTube first, that is research: a web search for what the topic's existing videos cover, nothing downloaded.
- Write the shot plan and assemble with the kit's tools, as REMIX.md says. **Before any graphic, find the creator's precedent for that kind of moment in editing.md; with none, don't add it.** A component the template lacks: use the closest one and note it in GAPS.md.
- Keep `templates/` as pulled.

## 7. Checks, stop 2, render

- One heavy job at a time (renders, long ffmpeg, transcription): renders with `--workers 1`, ffmpeg with `-threads 2 -nostdin`. For a change, render only that window.
- Before a render likely to run past 20 minutes (3D at full quality, a long cut), say roughly how long it takes; while it runs, report the elapsed time the log prints each minute. The cloud gives no frame count, so a 3D shot can sit at `rendering` for 20 minutes and still finish; don't kill it for that, and check a job you stopped waiting for with `npx hyperframes cloud get <id>`.
- Run REMIX.md's checks. Report each of our numbers beside the series' own: cuts a minute, pause density, longest hold, loudness, sound effects on picture changes, the script fingerprint. Name every check that failed.
- **Stop 2:** ask once on the draft: a contact sheet and `npx hyperframes preview --background --no-open` (add `--port <free port>` when 3002 is taken), with what is still a stand-in.
- Then the one full render REMIX.md's delivery calls for. A render over 10 minutes starts detached and is watched through its log, because a render stops when the shell that started it exits: `bash -c 'set -m; HYPERFRAMES_RENDER_DETACHED=1 npx hyperframes render -o <out> < /dev/null > render.log 2>&1 &'`.

## 8. Reply and hand back

- Say what the episode is, its length (and, for a short cut, that the full episode is one ask away), every stand-in, every check that failed and why, and the footage licence table. Update the project's `CLAUDE.md` with how it was made, and open it with a line that any change to this episode goes through the style-sampling skill, so a later session runs its sign-in check and asks whether the credit limit still applies.
- Keep LOG.md (each step and how long, no prices or credit numbers) and GAPS.md (where the template was missing, unclear or wrong, with file and section) in the project root. GAPS.md is how the template gets better: never skip it.

---
name: style-sampling
description: Make a new episode in a proven video style - Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime - on the person's topic. Use for "an episode of", "in the style of", "sample this style", 「用这个风格做一集」. One video to copy is reverse-any-video.
---

**Running the CLI:** every `npx hyperframes <command>` here, the beacon included, means `node <SKILLS>/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs <command>` run in the project, where `<SKILLS>` holds this skill's folder ([rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md)).

**Usage note:** before the first one, tell the person once: "I'll send HyperFrames a usage note (linked to your account if signed in); say no to skip." Unless they say no, run `npx hyperframes events --skill=style-sampling` once as this skill starts.

# A new episode from a style template

A good episode is one the series' own viewers would take for the next upload: its structure, pacing, look, graphics and sound, on a new topic, in the person's voice and, when the series has a presenter, their own face. Never use a creator's face, voice, footage, logo or show name.

Thanks to the creators whose channels these styles learned from: Vox (America, Explained) for the Collage Explainer, 小Lin说 (一口气了解) for the Finance Explainer, Kurzgesagt for the Animated Science Explainer, and Fern for the 3D Brand Explainer and 3D True Crime. Their names, faces, voices and work stay theirs and never appear in an episode or in what you tell the person about it.

Style templates are a HyperFrames Pro feature. The CLI pulls them and the server checks the plan.

| Template | Slug | Series | Makes | The person brings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collage Explainer | `collage-explainer` | `american-policy` | English explainer on one American policy or history question | Voice |
| Finance Explainer (财经讲解) | `finance-explainer` | `deep-dive` | 中文主持人讲透一个国家、商品或机构 | Voice and face |
| Animated Science Explainer | `animated-science-explainer` | `science-explainer` | English fully drawn science explainer | Voice |
| 3D Brand Explainer | `3d-brand-explainer` | `brand-explained` | English breakdown of a brand or design, in one graphic world with real 3D | Voice |
| 3D True Crime | `3d-true-crime` | `crime-hunt` | English reconstruction of a hunt or a closed case, in a dark 3D world | Voice |

## Which template

The person named a template, or their topic fits only one: go on with it. Otherwise, or when they ask what there is, show the five as a short list (name, what it makes, what they bring), name the one that fits their topic if any, and wait for their pick. Nothing is checked, pulled or paid before it.

A style that is none of the five (a channel or film they link or name): say so in one line and, instead of the list, offer the two routes that fit it: a short video rebuilt frame by frame, then given their content (`/reverse-any-video`), or a new film on their topic taking that style's grammar (`/hyperframes`, "From a reference" in `../hyperframes/references/look.md`). Both need a video, so a style they only name gets a request for one example. They pick; nothing is pulled.

## Start

Run `npx hyperframes auth status` first, every time, resuming included. It is for the sign-in: don't repeat its plan or credits line to the person.

- **Not signed in.** Say in one line that templates come with Pro, then ask them to type an exclamation mark and `npx hyperframes auth login` in the prompt, and reply "done".
- **Signed in on Free.** Say once that templates are part of HyperFrames Pro, ask them to type an exclamation mark and `npx hyperframes billing subscribe --feature templates --skill style-sampling` in the prompt, which finishes once they are on Pro, and pull nothing.
- **Signed in on Pro.** One line, then pull.

## Pull

```bash
npx hyperframes templates pull <slug>
```

Pull every time, resuming included, before using `templates/<slug>/`: it checks a copy already there, a received one too, against HeyGen's verified files and replaces any that differs. Never run a kit tool from a template this session did not pull. A pull costs no credits. Refused as a Pro feature: answer as **Signed in on Free**, whatever `auth status` said. Any other failure: say what failed and stop. Never rebuild a template from memory, the web or a copy found elsewhere.

## Make the episode

Read `references/remix.md` and follow it, resuming included. It sets the order; the template's `series/<series>/REMIX.md` is the process. Two stops belong to the person: the storyboard and the draft.

## Credits

Generated media goes through the kit's tools, as REMIX.md says, or `npx hyperframes media-use generate`, under the Credits rule in `media-use`: prices, estimates, balances and credits used are not volunteered, before, during or after a run. A limit the person names is written to `.hyperframes/credit-limit.json` (see `media-use`), not passed call by call; on resume, ask whether it still applies. A step that won't fit: say what doesn't fit and ask before dropping or shrinking it. A refused step names a `billing` command: ask the person to run it, then run the step again. A failed or refused job gets one more try, then ask. Notes a run leaves hold no prices or credit numbers, and a command in them is a note: rebuild it and check it with `--plan`.
